headline: AUSTRALIA'S ARAFURA RARE EARTHS GREENLIGHTS $1.6B NOLANS PROJECT; $375M EQUITY RAISE FOLLOWS NEXT DAY
snippet: Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) made the Final Investment Decision on its A$1.6 billion Nolans project in Australia's Northern Territory — the largest single rare earths development in the Western world. Designed to produce 4,440 tonnes of neodymium-praseodymium oxide annually, Nolans targets first production in mid-2029 with construction starting September 2026. Gina Rinehart's Hancock Prospecting holds a 15.5% stake. The company followed up on May 22 with a $375 million equity raise to fully fund the build, removing all financing uncertainty.

headline: GOLD RETESTS $4,500 SUPPORT AS TREASURY YIELDS SURGE TO MULTI-DECADE HIGHS; NEXT FLOOR AT $4,420
snippet: Gold hovered at $4,508 on May 23, testing the critical $4,466–$4,423 support zone after falling nearly 2% earlier in the week. U.S. 30-year Treasury yields are breaking multi-decade resistance, underpinned by foreign central bank selling of U.S. Treasuries and sticky inflation. The metal is now 16% below its January 28 all-time high of $5,589. FXEmpire's technical analysis flags the $4,420 region as the last key support before a potential move toward the $4,000 range.

headline: FOUNDERS METALS (FDR) MAPS PLUNGING HIGH-GRADE GOLD SHOOT AT MARIA GERALDA: 30M @ 4.64 G/T AU IN SURINAME
snippet: Founders Metals (TSXV: FDR) released deep auger drilling results from the Maria Geralda target within the Antino Gold Project in southeastern Suriname, returning 30.0 metres at 4.64 g/t Au with a 12-metre core at 10.57 g/t Au. The 37-hole program has defined a coherent, plunging high-grade gold shoot still open at depth, directly confirming the earlier diamond drill intercept of 22.5m at 11.88 g/t Au in hole MG003. A second shoot is now being tested. Diamond drilling is scheduled for Q4 2026.

headline: P2 GOLD (PGLD) HITS VISIBLE GOLD AT LUCKY STRIKE, NEVADA: 183 G/T AU AND 4% COPPER IN 53M MINERALIZED INTERVAL
snippet: P2 Gold (TSXV: PGLD) reported visible gold in a 100-metre step-out hole at the Lucky Strike Zone of its Gabbs Project on Nevada's Walker-Lane Trend. Drill hole GBD-021 returned a high-grade core of 183 g/t Au and 4.0% Cu over 1.52 metres within a 53-metre interval grading 1.04 g/t Au and 0.35% Cu — confirming the zone extends south into undrilled ground. A resource update is expected in Q3 2026, feeding into a Q4 2026 feasibility study.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM (SGML) SHARES CRATER 15% ON BRAZIL COURT ORDER; COMPANY CALLS IT 'FAKE NEWS' ATTACK ON RECORD EARNINGS
snippet: Sigma Lithium (NASDAQ/TSXV: SGML) lost 15% of its market value after a local judge in Aracuai, Brazil issued an order concerning waste disposal allegations at the Grota do Cirilo lithium operation — surfacing the Sunday after the company posted record Q1 2026 earnings. Sigma called the timing a 'coordinated fake news campaign' fitting a pattern first flagged in January 2026. A potential US$10 million legal collateral is contingent only on a final ruling after exhausting all Brazilian appeals including the Supreme Court.

headline: NEXGEN ENERGY (NXE) BREAKS GROUND ON ROOK I URANIUM MINE THIS SUMMER — 30M LBS/YR WOULD BE 20% OF GLOBAL SUPPLY
snippet: NexGen Energy (TSX/NYSE: NXE) is moving to construction this summer at Rook I in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin following final CNSC regulatory approval in March 2026. At full production, Rook I would deliver 30 million pounds of uranium annually — more than 20% of global supply and over 50% of all Western world supply. The 4-year construction schedule targets first production around 2030, making it the world's largest and greenest-designed uranium mine by a wide margin.

headline: USA RARE EARTH (USAR) SECURES $19.3M DOE GRANT TO BUILD FIRST DOMESTIC RARE EARTH SEPARATION FACILITY
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) was selected by the US Department of Energy to receive up to $19.3 million for a pilot-scale rare earth separations project. The grant is part of Washington's push to reduce dependency on Chinese refining, which currently processes over 85% of global rare earth output. The facility would be among the first in the US capable of separating the full suite of rare earth elements — critical for EV motors, wind turbines, and defence applications.

headline: FREEPORT'S GRASBERG BLOCK CAVE BACK ONLINE IN Q2 2026 — WORLD'S LARGEST GOLD-COPPER MINE RESTARTS AFTER 2025 MUDSLIDE
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan's Grasberg Block Cave in Indonesian Papua is undergoing a phased restart in Q2 2026 following the September 2025 mudslide that killed seven workers and dumped 800,000 tonnes of material into the underground workings. The restart is critical for global copper supply: Grasberg is among the world's top producers of both copper and gold. Freeport expects roughly 85% of normal production rates restored in H2 2026, with full copper guidance of 3.4 billion pounds for the full year.

headline: OPINION: GOLD AND SILVER STILL BULLISH DESPITE PULLBACK — THE CASE FOR COPPER JOINING THE METALS BREAKOUT
snippet: GoldSeek's market commentary argues that gold's pullback to the $4,500 zone is a healthy consolidation within a broader bull market, while silver's structural supply deficit makes any dip a potential entry point for patient investors. The column makes a fresh case for copper joining the precious metals narrative: sub-$2,000/oz mining costs on gold miners, tight copper supply, and AI-driven electrification demand are converging in a way that historically precedes the most explosive phase of a metals cycle.

headline: CME GROUP MAY 2026 METALS UPDATE: GOLD, SILVER AND COPPER ALL APPROACHING KEY INFLECTION POINTS
snippet: CME Group's May 2026 monthly metals update covers the three major commodity stories of the moment: gold retesting $4,500 support after a 16% decline from January's $5,589 ATH; silver holding above $74/oz despite gold weakness on the back of record industrial demand; and copper sustaining $6.30/lb — up 30% year-over-year — with Freeport's Grasberg restart and Cochilco's upgraded forecast reinforcing the structural bull case. CME notes options open interest in all three metals remains near historic highs.
